preserved_analysis.failure_mode_definition: A failure occurs when materially untrustworthy retrieved content is promoted into a factual answer whose authority or confidence exceeds the quality, independence, provenance, corroboration, contradiction state and proposition-level support of the available evidence. Deliberate source poisoning is one possible attack method, not a required structural condition.
preserved_analysis.failure_threshold: The threshold is met when a system converts source availability, superficial citation coverage or materially unreliable evidence into an affirmative factual claim without proportionate source-quality weighting, proposition-support checking, independence assessment, contradiction detection or corroboration. Synthetic origin alone does not satisfy the threshold.

severity_assessment.assessment_basis: S3: Materialised consequence: Mimikama documents a deliberately fabricated rabies-death story that was ingested into AI search answers and combined with an unrelated legitimate source, demonstrating adversarial content poisoning converted into authoritative-looking synthetic fact. Affected scope: the assessment is confined to the people, systems, organisations, service cohort, and time period expressly identified in this occurrence; it does not extrapolate to unreported users or hypothetical future harm. Seriousness and reversibility or persistence: The consequence is meaningful but bounded, substantially reversible, or not shown to be grave. Quantitative information: No reliable affected-person, duration, financial-loss, or other scale total is preserved beyond the stated occurrence facts. Evidentiary limits: The poisoning campaign was not independently reproduced. The record concerns factual-source authority, not instruction-following authority. S3 rather than S2 is appropriate because substantial or grave lasting harm is not established; S3 rather than S4 is appropriate because the realised consequence exceeds a minor transient inconvenience.
